newsitem.title: FRANCE: France asked EU to sell more wheat, official says.
newsitem.headline: France asked EU to sell more wheat, official says.

text.p: A top French agricultural official said on Thursday that France had sought and obtained a more "dynamic" export policy for wheat from the European Commission in the past two weeks.

"It is clear that over the past two weeks the Commission has, at France's request, been running a more dynamic export policy and has been increasing the awards of its weekly certificates," Pierre-Olivier Drege, director general of the French farm ministry, told Reuters.
He was commenting on news that traders had doubled the volume of export bids placed through France at a weekly European Union export tender, bidding for more than 1.3 million tonnes.
Drege said France hoped the European Commission would maximise grain sales but without disrupting the world market.

"Our wish is to maintain a balance between quantities which are significant enough to do what can be done in the first half of the campaign, without putting too much pressure on a world market which is already disrupted by large Argentine exports," he said.
"Argentine exports should fade out at the end of the year because a large part of their crop has already been sold."
Drege was speaking at a grain industry event in Paris.
